MOLECULAR PATHOLOGY REPORT
[redacted location] Cancer Center
Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine

Patient Name: [redacted name]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Ordering Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Diagnosis: Metastatic adenocarcinoma of lung
Specimen Type: EBUS-guided transbronchial needle aspiration
Tumor Content: 30%

TEST PERFORMED
Cancer Hotspot Panel - DNA Analysis
Test Code: [redacted ID]

METHODOLOGY
Amplicon-based next-generation sequencing (NGS) was performed for targeted analysis of cancer-associated genes. The assay utilizes PCR amplification of specific genomic regions followed by sequencing on a high-throughput platform. Data processing was performed using our standard bioinformatics pipeline, which includes:
• Read alignment to human reference genome (GRCh38)
• Variant calling using multiple algorithms
• Annotation and filtering of variants

Analytical Sensitivity: The assay reliably detects variants at ≥2.5% allele frequency with minimum coverage of 15 reads
Genes Analyzed: EGFR (exons 18-21), KRAS (codons 12, 13, 59, 61, 117, 146), BRAF (codons 443-474 and 582-608)

RESULTS

GENE-SPECIFIC FINDINGS:

EGFR (NM_005228.5)
Exons analyzed: 18-21
Result: No pathogenic variants detected
Coverage: Adequate (mean coverage >500x)

KRAS (NM_033360.4)
Codons analyzed: 12, 13, 59, 61, 117, 146
Result: No pathogenic variants detected
Coverage: Adequate (mean coverage >500x)

BRAF (NM_004333.6)
Codons analyzed: 443-474, 582-608
Result: No pathogenic variants detected
Coverage: Adequate (mean coverage >500x)

STRUCTURAL VARIANT ANALYSIS
RNA panel for fusion detection: Not performed due to insufficient material

INTERPRETATION
No targetable mutations were identified in the EGFR, KRAS, or BRAF genes. The absence of activating mutations in these genes suggests that the patient is unlikely to benefit from:
• EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (e.g., erlotinib, gefitinib, osimertinib)
• MEK inhibitors (e.g., trametinib)
• BRAF inhibitors (e.g., dabrafenib)

The actionability for ALK/ROS1/RET/MET/NTRK inhibitor therapy remains undetermined due to insufficient material for RNA-based fusion analysis.

LIMITATIONS
• This assay is limited to the detection of variants in the specified regions of EGFR, KRAS, and BRAF genes
• Structural variants, including gene fusions, require RNA-based analysis which could not be performed
• Low-level variants below 2.5% allele frequency may not be detected
• Complex insertions/deletions >15bp may not be reliably detected

RECOMMENDATIONS
Consider repeat testing with a separate biopsy specimen if clinically indicated, particularly to assess for targetable gene fusions (ALK, ROS1, RET, MET, NTRK) that require RNA analysis.

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Cancer Center Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA.

Electronically signed by:
[redacted name], MD, PhD
Board Certified in Molecular Genetic Pathology
Date: [redacted date]
